request.spec:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added patrons and backing, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**How it works on screen**
- Each person's row now has three new columns:
  - **Patrons:** the names, sorted and separated by ", ".
  - **Backing:** the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping any that are n/a, and 0.00 with no patrons.
  - **A picker and "Add patron" button:** adds one patron at a time.
- The picker only lists people the person could name, so it never offers the person themselves or someone who is already their patron.
- The server also refuses those two cases, a person not on the sheet, and an empty choice. A refusal shows an error on the row (`person-patron-error`), writes nothing to the store, and adds nothing to the audit file. The error clears when the picker is changed or the next action on that row is taken.
- Backing is worked out in the browser from the same due-totals the row already shows. So a held patron counts at their current due-total, which can be 0.00.

**Stored data and server**
- A new table, `person_patron`, holds each person–patron pair at most once (migration `V19__person_patron.sql`).
- A new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/patrons`, adds a patron. It writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> patron=<patron name>` to the audit file.
- Each person sent to the front end now includes their patrons' names, sorted.

**Front end**
- The new columns are in `features/patrons/patrons.slot.tsx`.
- To reuse the due-total calculation, I changed `useDueTotals` in `rates.slot.tsx` from private to exported.

**Choices the request didn't settle**
- Backing matches patrons by name rather than id. That's safe because names are unique on a sheet.
- Retired people can still be named as patrons, and their due-totals count towards backing.
- Adding a patron doesn't change the person's edit version and doesn't write a ROLLUP line, which matches the audit records the test expects.
